reading.body:
Flexential Portland - Hillsboro 5 publishes 36 MW of IT capacity across 358,000 square feet, making it Oregon's largest single facility by disclosed power, though only six of Oregon's 133 mapped data centers report megawatt figures at all.

At typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, 36 MW supports roughly 900 racks. At colocation density of 10 kW per rack, it supports roughly 3,600 racks. The low power density per square foot suggests the facility is built for mixed workloads rather than purpose-built GPU clusters. The operator has not published a breakdown of actual tenant composition or current utilization, so the facility's role in AI infrastructure remains unspecified.

The certification stack, which includes SOC 2 Type II, PCI DSS, ITAR, NIST 800-53, and HITRUST, qualifies the campus for regulated workloads across finance, defense, and healthcare. These certifications address operational controls and data handling standards, not compute density or power delivery infrastructure. They indicate the facility can serve regulated AI customers, but do not constrain or enable any particular workload type.

Oregon publishes 182 MW across six facilities with reported capacity figures. This represents only a fraction of the 133 facilities OpenStreetMap records in the state. The grid's current capacity to support AI scaling in Oregon, and how this facility's power draw relates to regional constraints, are not addressed in operator specifications and remain unassessed.
